content:
marta: Heads-up — noticed a latency regression on small-seq requests when FlashAttention + paged KV are enabled. Batch formation is pausing (~20–40ms) waiting for kernel selection to settle and then falling back to the slower kernel, which kills P50 for <32-token calls.

sam: Ugh. Seen similar in the staging trace dump? Any flame/profile snippets? :eyes:

marta: Pushed a short trace to the runbook: https://internal/runbooks/1850001111 (private). Key snippet: kernel_select latency spikes when paged-kv page miss rate > 0.12 and batch contains mixed seq-lens.

ryan: Quick idea — add a fast-path in the continuous batcher: if estimated seq_len distribution median < 48 and paged-kv miss_rate > threshold, force small-seq kernel with a token_budget cap. That avoids swapping to the Flash kernel mid-batch.

ana: (typo) ana: I like force-small-seq, but we should keep cost control. Suggest config knobs: token_budget_target, kernel_switch_penalty_ms, and a small_seq_headroom_pct.

sam: Posting a proposed config patch we tested locally:

```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  token_budget_target: 1200          # tokens across forming batch
  small_seq_threshold: 48           # tokens considered "short"
  small_seq_headroom_pct: 15        # allow 15% extra to avoid premature flush
  kernel_switch_penalty_ms: 25      # prefer avoiding kernel swap if it would add <25ms
  paging_miss_rate_threshold: 0.12
  force_small_seq_kernel_when:
    - median_seq_len < small_seq_threshold
    - paging_miss_rate > paging_miss_rate_threshold
```

chris: Tested this with the repro harness (nvprof + batcher debug). Results: P50 down from 18.6ms -> 13.2ms on g4dn-equivalent; P95 unchanged. Energy/cost impact negligible.

marta: Nice. Two open questions: 1) interaction with dynamic batching (we have bursty short requests that we still want to coalesce), and 2) safety for mixed-model routing where kernel compat differs.

ryan: For #1: use a two-tier queue: short-queue and mixed-queue. Short-queue has tighter token_budget but longer wait cap (to allow coalescing) and honors force_small_seq_kernel. Mixed-queue goes through normal kernel selection.

ana: For #2: ensure kernel capability flags are checked before forcing. If model lacks small-seq optimized kernel, fallback to default. Also add metric: kernel_forced_rate and avg_switch_cost_ms.

infra-bot: deploy-batcher-canary: canary rollout started for batcher v2.4.1 -> 4 hosts (region-us-west-2).

sam: Another profiling detail: when paged-kv miss_rate > ~0.2 we see sustained kernel thrash because the runtime attempts Flash kernels but page faults cause long waits. Maybe add early-bail: if page miss trend rising, route those requests to dedicated paged-KV nodes or increase prefetch window.

marta: Agree. For the near-term patch let's do: add force_small_seq_kernel rule + kernel_switch_penalty_ms + metrics. We'll coordinate a canary with 10% traffic and monitor kernel_forced_rate, p50/p95, and page_miss_rate.

chris: I'll prepare the canary dashboard and alert thresholds. Want to track: batch_wait_ms, kernel_select_ms, page_miss_rate, kernel_forced_rate, cost_token_perk.

ana: I'll add unit tests for hybrid batches (mix of seq lengths) and a perf integration test that simulates page-miss spikes.

marta: Thanks. I'll open the PR and link the test harness. Planning to merge Tue AM if canary looks good. :thumbsup:

sam: One more note — document the behavior in the runtime docs under "batcher kernel heuristics" so oncall knows the new tradeoffs.

marta: Will do.

chris: Canary dashboards ready: https://internal/dash/1850001111-canary (read-only).

marta: Launching canary now.

infra-bot: deploy-batcher-canary: canary rollout complete (4 hosts). monitoring hooks active.

chris: Early signal (5m): kernel_forced_rate ~ 12%, p50 improved to 12.9ms, page_miss_rate unchanged. No alerts yet.

marta: Good first pass. Will keep watching for 2h and then widen to 50% if stable.
